actions.description: Control: `manager` is the position where the connector does return `name`.

The bug: `reports` is the position where the connector returns only `id`, so `name` is null. Expansion unioned the two positions of `Person`, so the planner served this from the `users` connector instead of the `Query.person` entity resolver.
Both positions in one query, which is the clearest statement of the defect: the same field on the same type resolves differently depending on the path it was reached by.

Source-aware, control: `manager` still resolves from the `users` connector in a single fetch. The entity resolver returns "Ada (via resolver)" for person 9, so getting plain "Ada" here proves the restriction did NOT manufacture an unnecessary re-entry at a position the connector can serve.

Source-aware, the fix: `reports` is restricted to `{ id }`, so `name` is resolved by re-entering `Query.person`. "Grace" comes from GET /people/2 and could not have come from the `users` connector, which never returns a name under `reports`.

Source-aware, both positions in one query — the same statement as the expansion-path case above, now answered correctly: `name` resolves per position, from the connector under `manager` and from the entity resolver under `reports`.

Source-aware: `title` is returned at neither position, so even `manager` needs the re-entry here. This is what distinguishes a genuinely per-position restriction from one that only happened to fix `reports`.
